extraction.name: MMMU: A Massive Multi-discipline Multimodal Understanding and Reasoning Benchmark for Expert AGI
extraction.description: MMMU is a benchmark designed to evaluate multimodal models on massive multi-discipline tasks demanding college-level subject knowledge and deliberate reasoning. It includes 11.5K meticulously collected multimodal questions from college exams, quizzes, and textbooks, covering six core disciplines: Art & Design, Business, Science, Health & Medicine, Humanities & Social Science, and Tech & Engineering. These questions span 30 subjects and 183 subfields, comprising 30 highly heterogeneous image types.
extraction.creator: Xiang Yue, Yuansheng Ni, Kai Zhang, Tianyu Zheng, Ruoqi Liu, Ge Zhang, Samuel Stevens, Dongfu Jiang, Weiming Ren, Yuxuan Sun, Cong Wei, Botao Yu, Ruibin Yuan, Renliang Sun, Ming Yin, Boyuan Zheng, Zhenzhu Yang, Yibo Liu, Wenhao Huang, Huan Sun, Yu Su, Wenhu Chen
extraction.citeAs: Xiang Yue, Yuansheng Ni, Kai Zhang, Tianyu Zheng, Ruoqi Liu, Ge Zhang, Samuel Stevens, Dongfu Jiang, Weiming Ren, Yuxuan Sun, Cong Wei, Botao Yu, Ruibin Yuan, Renliang Sun, Ming Yin, Boyuan Zheng, Zhenzhu Yang, Yibo Liu, Wenhao Huang, Huan Sun, Yu Su, Wenhu Chen. extraction.rai:dataCollection: Data is primarily collected from free online resources, quizzes, textbooks, and other study materials. Over 50 university students, including co-authors, specializing in the 30 subjects assisted in question collection. They collected multimodal questions from major textbooks and online resources, creating new questions based on their expertise where necessary. The annotators were instructed to adhere to copyright and license regulations, avoiding data from sites prohibiting copy and redistribution. Given data contamination concerns, annotators were advised to select questions without immediately available answers, such as those with answers in separate documents or at the end of textbooks.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Manual Human Curator, Document analysis, Web Scraping
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Questions sourced from college exams, quizzes, textbooks, and online resources across 30 subjects spanning six disciplines: Art & Design, Business, Science, Health & Medicine, Humanities & Social Science, and Tech & Engineering.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Data quality control was performed in multiple stages: (1) Lexical overlap and source URL similarity were employed to identify potential duplicate problems, which were then reviewed by authors to eliminate duplications. (2) Problems were distributed among co-authors for format and typo checking, ensuring adherence to a standardized format with necessary corrections. (3) Authors categorized problems into four difficulty levels (very easy, easy, medium, hard), and approximately 10% classified as very easy were excluded from the benchmark.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotators collected multimodal questions and annotated all fields including the question, answer options for multiple-choice questions, the correct answer, image types, question difficulty, and explanation (if available). Questions were categorized as either multiple-choice or open-ended. All questions were required to contain one or more images, be written in English, meet college-level difficulty, and be unambiguous. Each collected sample was stored in a separate JSON file following a standard naming convention.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: A user-friendly web interface was developed for data annotation and verification.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset is divided into a few-shot development set (5 questions per subject), a validation set (approximately 900 questions), and a test set (10,500 questions). A live-updating leaderboard is available at https://mmmu-benchmark.github.io/#leaderboard. Version changes are documented, with updates including additional model results and corrections.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: MMMU is designed to push the boundaries of what large multimodal models can achieve and is intended to be instrumental in developing next-generation multimodal foundation models and monitoring progress towards Expert AGI. The benchmark aims to evaluate models on tasks akin to those faced by experts, testing both breadth (covering diverse disciplines) and depth (requiring expert-level reasoning).
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The manual curation process may carry biases. The focus on college-level subjects might not be sufficient for testing Expert AGI comprehensively. MMMU combines multiple-choice questions with concise open-ended questions to balance complexity and practicality, but this may not capture all aspects of expert-level performance. The benchmark does not provide a direct mapping between performance on MMMU and the 90th percentile of skilled adults as defined in AGI taxonomy.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: MMMU is designed for evaluating large multimodal models on college-level multi-discipline multimodal understanding and reasoning tasks. Use cases include Testing and Validation of multimodal foundation models. The benchmark is intended to assess models' capabilities in expert-level perception, knowledge recall, and reasoning across diverse academic disciplines.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: For multiple-choice questions: one correct answer from provided options. For open-ended questions: one correct short answer. Explanations are provided for 2,035 questions (17.62% of the dataset).
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Over 50 college students (including co-authors) from various disciplines and subjects, specializing in the 30 subjects covered in the benchmark.
